messages:
sara_support: FYI customer (acct acme-inc) hit a case where our autorouter picked the wrong tool. They called the payments endpoint to issue a refund but the invocation routed to `credit_v2` which created a credit note. Payload + router debug below. Can we triage? :eyes:

sara_support: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"customer_id":"acme-123","amount":120.00,"currency":"USD","reason":"returned item","origin":"support_ui"}'```

sara_support: router.debug output: ```route_input: {amount:120, currency:USD, reason:returned item, origin:support_ui}
candidates:
 - credit_v2 (score=0.71) tags:[financial,credit,note] signatures:[amount,currency,reason]
 - refund (score=0.68) tags:[financial,refund] signatures:[amount,currency,reason,method]
selected: credit_v2 (fallback_policy=prefer_higher_score)```

james_oncall: ack, grabbing logs & customer request id. Do we have the raw request id?

sara_support: request_id=ron-20260315-3342. Customer says it happened 2x in last 24h. Workaround was to call support UI flow and choose 'issue refund' manually.

kevin_engineer: I can repro locally. This looks like a suffix/signature collision between `credit_v2` and `refund`. Both share the same minimal surface (amount,currency,reason) so our fuzzy scorer slightly favors `credit_v2` because of tag weight and a longer usage history -> higher prior.

kevin_engineer: Quick notes: router uses tokenized name + signatures + tag priors. `credit_v2` has tags [financial, credit] and an alias `credit` which bumps its prior on these payloads. `refund` lacks an explicit alias and lower tag weight.

lena_support: what's the immediate mitigation for the customer? They need refunds processed ASAP.

kevin_engineer: short-term: include an explicit hint to force refund: add `intent":"refund"` or `tool_hint":"refund"` in JSON body. Our router will treat explicit tool_hint as a hard bias. Example: ```{"customer_id":"acme-123","amount":120.00,"currency":"USD","intent":"refund"}```

kevin_engineer: medium-term: I'll propose two changes: 1) add canonical aliases for `refund` (alias `refund`, tag weight +2), 2) adjust priority to prefer tools tagged with `refund` semantics when a `reason` contains refund-like tokens (refund, returned, chargeback). I'll open a PR.

deploy_bot: PR #842 opened by kevin_engineer: "router: lower alias prior for credit_v2, add refund alias & phrase matcher" -> CI passed. Staging deploy queued.

mike_pm: please add a short note in the customer ticket and ping the AE. AE contact is @ana. We should also ask if they want us to retroactively void the credit note.

kevin_engineer: staging deploy completed, #842 applied to staging. I ran the same curl repro against staging -> router now selects `refund` (score=0.92). Log: ```selected: refund (score=0.92)```

opsbot: automated note: staging->canary rollout for router config change started (id: rtr-20260315-842). Monitoring logs for anomalies.

sara_support: tested workaround with the customer (they added intent) and it worked. Customer accepted we can reverse the accidental credit; they'll wait for ops to confirm before we undo. :ok_hand:

lena_support: leaving note for billing ops to reverse credit note if approved by AE.

mike_pm: assigning follow-up: confirm canary metrics (false positive/negative rates) for 24h, escalate to ops if anything >1%.

kevin_engineer: will follow up with a small postmortem and add unit tests for alias collisions. PR -> #842 merged to main after canary validated.

sara_support: closing loop with customer, they said thanks. Will re-open if recurrence.
